posts.title: LEGO Star Wars Set Discussion 2026 - READ FIRST POST!!!
posts.text: The droid arm attachment is an interesting part with a lot of applications for Star Wars characters and also a lot of applications for general building. I look forward to the New Elementary analysis of the part, and to seeing how else it gets used in retail sets. I'm usually not very interested in lightsaber duel sets, but I hoped this Mustafar duel would finally be a set I'd want to buy. Eh, meh. The Cloud City duel looks just fine, though. The Endor battlepack is so bad. Every year I hope there will be a straight remake of the original Speeder Bikes set from 1999 and every year I'm disappointed. That set was perfect and it seems like such a no-brainer to keep re-releasing it at a battlepack price point, with a couple of Rebel troopers substituted for Luke if you don't like getting too many copies of named characters. The Y-wing looks great. The proportions and detailing are better than any previous playscale Y-wing. I like how the droid has been re-oriented to face forward for the first time in 20 years. The new windscreen element looks like it has the same excellent dual-molding as the new Snowspeeder windscreen, even though the shape still isn't perfect for a Y-wing. (Still waiting for a Hoth snowspeeder with the new windscreen!) The original 1999 windscreen element always worked better for the Y-wing than for the X-wing, and better for the X-wing than for the Snowspeeder, so it's a little sad to see it replaced on all three vehicles after so long. I hope the new Snowspeeder and Y-wing windscreens get many years of use across many varieties of swooshies. The 2015 X-wing windscreen has been a slam-dunk of a design, incredibly versatile and used on a wide range of other vehicles.

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: You absolutely should. I know people who had entirely tuned out of marvel and are loving it. (Is Seven Havens as good as ATLA? I liked ATLA a lot and thought Korra S1 was OK, but couldn't get through S2.) I would assume so. It'll be nice to see the images- a lot of the builds for these sets are wholly up in the air, and some figures as well- which scarlet spider, is a figure-scaled Jeff included with the statue, etc. I have seen that, and I do like the way of adding complexity to bullseye being that they've simply made him decide he's a "good guy" now without changing the fact that he's a psycho serial killer- that is entirely in character-, but I'm not a huge fan of the inversion they've gone with. Typically Fisk is the one that can be reasoned/bargained with, even trying to go legit at points, whereas Bullseye is Daredevil's Joker, the one who's constantly pushing him to break his rule. In the specific situation of Born Again where Kingpin holding a municipal position somehow gives him the powers of the god-emperor of mankind, I can understand that maybe Fisk is a bigger priority, but it's still weird to see any situation in which they're fighting alongside eachother.

posts.title: [MOC] - Return of the La-15
posts.text: This is not an upgraded old MOC - instead, I redesigned my La-15 from the ground up! I disassembled the old La-15 to build my version of the TIE Bomber. Now this rather obscure aircraft returns as an entirely new model! Instead of constructing the fuselage arond 1x1 SNOT bricks, I opted for a simpler yet more effective brackets+curved slopes solution. The wings are now brick-built and studless, although the same cannot be said about the horizontal stabilizer. Cannons aren't represented by stickers anymore, but rather by actual parts. The wing fences are... still represented by flexible tubes... Of course, the cockpit interior is detailed (and fits a pilot minifigure)... ...And the landing gear is retractable! Now, I need your honest opinion: do you think this new version is an upgrade over the old one or a downgrade? Please let me know! P. S. : sorry for the crude hand-made stickers...

posts.title: So, what Do people want?
posts.text: - A return of the 'Fun At The...' Minifigure sets - to give a wider variety of figures available for more specific activities and environments (e.g. fun at the ski lodge, fun at the wedding, fun at the water park, fund at the skating rink)... - Lettering bricks - Square tiles with a right angle and opposite curve that complement the existing rounded tiles - Useful printed parts in modular sets (e.g. Travel posters or a World map for a travel agency) - World Flags like in Set 242 'International Flags' - these can be based on World Cup participating teams to avoid seemingly favouring particular nations above others - Safari sets in City (and other wildlife sets) - not released in one sole wave never to be seen again though, give us a new one each wave and within a couple of years we'll have all the main missing animals (giraffe, hippo + baby, zebra, rhino, gazelle, meerkat, hyena...) - Return of the Adventurers (or at least a tribute set using all the original hieroglyphic pieces - don't you even dare try doing it with stickers, Lego) - Stop making Lego less fun in feeling that it needs to be bought only at certain times to get value for money (e.g. when a particular GWP is available or double points). I just want to buy it throughout the year and not feel I'm missing out and have to wait for a better deal - it's taking all the enjoyment from being a Lego hobbyist these days. - More animals in CMF series (including baby versions of bigger animals) - More variety with trains - don't just release big train sets but smaller sets to allow collectors to buy additional carriages, plus other train-related items like bridges, signals, track that can incline. Otherwise if you must release large sets, please base them in more interesting locations like an Andean or Outback Train and include animals (e.g. llamas or kangaroos)... - Stop cheapening sets with stickers (Yuck! ) - Less of the sets increasing in size all the times and at an equally unaffordable cost (storage space is a big issue for long-term fans). For example, sets like the gorilla set didn't need the enormous helicopter and the Venetian Neighbourhood didn't need a non-Lego piano piece, thus increasing the price even more. Stop being so unpleasantly greedy Lego - you have lost my respect as a company and I spend far less than nowadays that I did before as a result. It feels like you only cater for the Johnny-come-lately fans these days.

posts.title: Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: @Bliss Another idea just popped in there :D The non-LEGO interface "ecosystem" of LEGO Blockly (to connect to selected LEGO interfaces, e.g., Int.A, PF, Cubes) consists of ESP32 based microcontrollers. How about making a "generic" LEGO Blockly ESP32 based interface, e.g., using the beloved WROOM 32 DevKit 1 boards? 4 or more inputs (GPIOs), just A/D conversion (no Wifi = multiplexed ADC1+2 available). 4 or more inputs - just digital. 6 or more outputs. Reasoning: TLG only made "some" types of sensors. They are generally rather bulky, particularly the later generations (need to be for ruggedness and data handling), and are expensive. Furthermore, most LEGO interfaces except Int.B have max. 3 inputs and outputs. And Interface B costs a fortune - you can easily get about 30+ ESP boards for one Int.B There are also myriads of dead cheap sensors out there, which are or can be made ESP32 compatible With the super-small H bridge modules, even motors can be attached; e.g. 4.5V LEGO motors (using 5V USB power supply). You don't have to, if you just want to drive VIS LEDs ... When using C3's or the like, they could be placed anywhere (where there is USB power) and serve as "remote sensors". In this case the number of GPIOs is restricted, of course. Optionally (and not really needed) you could even add OLED displays to such generic ESP32 servers, and LEGO Blockly would do the text output ... Just an idea ... Best Thorsten

posts.title: [Help for MOC] Lego City Hyper Tower (inspired by Lego City Tower 60473)
posts.text: Hello, When the LEGO City Tower came out, I really liked the Idea, but always felt there was too less of everything. So I was thinking about how far one could take that. For sure this isn't a typical set which fits in a big organized AFOL City. I see it more as a standalone crazy city diorama or a really fun play set. I would really like to build the set by myself, but I'm lacking the time to design this several thousand pieces set. I've got a really detailed concept and have built a very rough model in studio2.0 as a proof of concept and size. The only limit I've set for this set is width of below 75 studs. So my question is, is anyone crazy enough to join me or take over this project? My idea adds some basic unspectacular things as well as some insane plot twists. Ground floor The center this time isn't the subway but a little museum. This exhibits at least a mid sized dinosaur (Raptor or Small T Rex), a historic figure like a Knight or Mummy, something worthy behind a laser grid like a diamond or so. On its right hand there is a 8 studs wide garage for a fire engine. But this time a real one, not a small car. Still 6 studs wide but with an extendable ladder, a real hose, and big bay for some tools. Seats two. Still compact but full of features. Next to it a police station. Also with a 8 Studs wide garage but also a little Office and jail next to it, accessible from the side. The police car would still be racecar like, 6 Studs, but with a backseat for the villain. The jail has some kind of breakout funktion, like exploding a wall with dynamite or so. The office has a computer, some donuts. On the left side of the museum there's a small car workshop / tuning garage. Theres a racecar in an equal kind like the police car, features a backseat or more like a trunk. This could be taken for races or maybe a robber steals it to escape. The tuning workshop can make the racecars off-road cars with bigger wheels or make them flying cars by replacing wheels with impellers. The building ends here, but left to it there's now real railroad track instead of a subway. With a small 2-3 studs platform for passengers to board the train. Right above the railroads there is a large crane. It's legs are directly left and right from the railroad, so the train passes through it. Directly left from the crane and railroad there is a small parallel wharf where container ship can dock. There's also a lifebuoy and someone with a fishing rod, but I guess only a shark and maybe an octopuses is included in this set so stay cautious. I've also heard rumors there's a treasure chest somewhere in the sea. The set features unique containers system with 6x12 Studs Containers with roof sloped to the sides. Some are for different cargo, some are for passengers (at least 6 per container). The crane can load these containers to the train, cargo ship and a container truck. The train consists of two power cars with one aerodynamical driver cabin on each, end and each can load a container which sits flush on it with the same sloped roofline. This way it can be used as a passenger or cargo train. The cargo ship is rather compact and 12 studs wide but loads 2 or 3 containers. It features small cabin with at least bed and a place to cook, likely more, as well as a small command bridge for 2. Since the 12 wide containers have to stand on top the 12 wide ship, below the containers theres are hatches which open up an additional cargo hold inside the ship. As if that isn't enough, it can also slide out a ramp for cars and act as a small ferry too. It also has a small crane to unload things on its own. There is also little submarine seating one, which also is 6x12 in size and can be loaded like a container to the truck, train and in every case the ship, transforming it into a research ship.
